title: Decision tree computes the junta restriction
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on $n$ coordinates, let $P$ be a set of coordinates, and fix a sign assignment $z$ on $P$. If a decision tree querying only coordinates outside $P$ is not classified as a bad output for $(f,P,z)$, then on every binary input whose sign vector agrees with $z$ on $P$, the tree returns the value of $f$ at that sign vector.

$P$ is a finite set of coordinates among the $n$ coordinates
$z$ assigns a sign to each coordinate in $P$
